title: Deleting a user keeps their articles with a null author, while their comments, follows and favorites are deleted.
content:
articles.author_id references users.id with ondelete SET NULL and is nullable. The commentaries, favorites and followers_to_followings foreign keys to users use ondelete CASCADE instead.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: articlesCount in list responses is the number of articles on the current page, not the total match count.
content:
list_articles returns articles_count=len(articles) after a LIMIT/OFFSET query. No separate count query is run.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

title: Invalid tokens and unknown token users are rejected with 403, not 401.
content:
_get_current_user raises HTTP 403 with could not validate credentials when the token cannot be decoded and when its username no longer exists. Wrong header prefixes also return 403.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90

title: Only the article author may update or delete an article, checked by username equality.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares article.author.username with the current user's username. check_article_modification_permissions raises 403 when they differ, and the SQL update and delete also filter on author_id.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
app/app/services/security.py builds a CryptContext with the bcrypt scheme and deprecated=auto, and uses it to hash and verify passwords.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: All API models expose snake_case fields as camelCase JSON aliases.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name, so fields like articles_count serialize as articlesCount. Renaming a Python field changes the public JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: The user feed is ordered by article created_at ascending, oldest first.
content:
The get-articles-for-feed SQL joins followed authors and orders by a.created_at with no DESC keyword, then applies LIMIT and OFFSET.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/articles.sql:113

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one HTTPException with incorrect email or password and raises it both when the email lookup fails and when check_password fails.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: Adding a favorite is an idempotent insert that ignores conflicts on the composite primary key.
content:
add-article-to-favorites inserts into favorites with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, relying on the (user_id, article_id) primary key. Tag creation and article-tag links use the same pattern.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/articles.sql:5

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm using the app secret key.
content:
app/app/services/jwt.py sets ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode tokens and as the only accepted algorithm on decode. The same secret_key signs and verifies, so anyone holding it can mint tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue and there is no refresh token.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user passes it as the expiry delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The token identifies the user by username, not by user id.
content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only the username into the payload, and _get_current_user looks the user up by that username. Changing a username makes old tokens fail, which is why the update-user route issues a new token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Article list pagination defaults to limit 20 and offset 0, with a lower bound on limit but no upper bound.
content:
ArticlesFilters declares limit with default 20 and ge=1, and offset with ge=0. The query dependency repeats the same bounds, so a client can request any large limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:42

title: Database access uses named raw SQL files loaded by aiosql on asyncpg, with no ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in app/app/db/queries/sql with the asyncpg adapter, and repositories call the named queries. Only filter_articles builds SQL dynamically with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: A separate per-user salt is stored in its own column and prepended to the password before hashing.
content:
UserInDB.change_password generates a salt with bcrypt.gensalt, stores it in users.salt, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same salt, so the salt column cannot be dropped or changed without breaking logins.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
content:
update_article_by_slug computes a new slug from the new title when a title is given and passes it to the repository, which writes it to articles.slug. The update route does not run the duplicate-slug check that create runs.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify, so two articles cannot share a title slug.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The create route checks whether that slug exists and returns 400 article already exists, and articles.slug is a unique column.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.
content:
AppSettings.jwt_token_prefix defaults to Token. _get_authorization_header splits the header on a space and rejects any other prefix with 403 unsupported authorization type.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on users, articles and commentaries. The repositories read updated_at back from RETURNING.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
